keep stirring so no lumps remain, and the mixture is smooth
lower the heat, cover the pan with a lid and cook it for five minutes
switch off the heat, take the pot off and mix it up once more
transfer the mixture onto a wide plate and allow it to cool
add jeera, grated coconut, butter and salt to taste if required
mix well, knead it with your fingers so that the mixture comes together in a ball
pinch off lemon sized portions and roll them between your palms to make balls
repeat this till no mixture remains
place the prepared balls in a steamer or idli stand of a pressure cooker and steam them like you would steam idlis

content.summary: The everyday Tamil household ven pongal: dal lightly roasted, cooked soft with rice in a pressure cooker, finished with a generous ghee tempering of pepper, cumin, ginger, cashew, curry leaves and asafoetida.
content.intro: This is the plain, temple-safe version - no onion, no garlic, no chilli. The two things that decide success are the water ratio (keep it loose) and a hot, unhurried tempering.
tips: Roast the moong dal only until it smells nutty - colour barely changes.
Crush the peppercorns lightly so the heat spreads.
Keep a small cup of hot water aside to loosen the pongal just before serving.
common_mistakes: Too little water - pongal sets hard as it cools.
Tempering in ghee that is not hot enough - spices go soft and the aroma is flat.
Serving late - always thickens on standing.
content.serving_suggestions: Serve hot with coconut chutney and either sambar or a tangy brinjal gothsu.

steps.action: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pan over medium heat until it smells nutty and turns pale gold, about 3 minutes.
Rinse the rice and the roasted dal together in a couple of changes of water and drain.
Add the rinsed rice and dal to the pressure cooker with the water, close, and cook on medium for 4 whistles. Let the pressure fall on its own.
While the cooker cools, heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers.

params.until_condition: ghee shimmers; a cumin seed sizzles on contact

steps.action: Add the crushed pepper and cumin, let them crackle, then the cashews until golden, then the ginger, curry leaves and asafoetida for a few seconds.
Open the cooker, add salt, and mash the rice and dal lightly. Pour in the tempering with all its ghee and fold through, loosening with a little hot water to a soft dropping consistency.

params.until_condition: soft, creamy, falls slowly off a spoon

steps.action: Serve hot straight away, with an extra tsp of ghee on top if you like, alongside coconut chutney and sambar.
